name: Hare
idea: A walker that runs. Same six spoked legs as the league, but a light frame, full-size motors and a gait driven at more than twice the league's pace, with a steel lance held out ahead. It strikes at a run, where a blow breaks joints, and is gone before the enemy has turned.

name: Lever
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Warden, Mantis), including the champion.
idea: Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Wasp
idea: Speed as the weapon. A 430 kg wheeled wedge that goes three times as fast as anything in the league, hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Bolt
idea: Wasp from round 1 rebuilt for a small ring, where there is no room to reach top speed: six wheels on full-size motors for pull-away, thick steel axles, and runs that start from seven metres out. A wheeled wedge that hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Jab
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Dreadnought, Strider), including the champion.
idea: A boxer that goes for the legs. Every machine in the league stands on spoked legs whose joints are its weakest, and a blow counts by how fast it lands, so this machine carries three piston fists that strike at 8 m/s whatever its own speed. It picks the nearest leg still attached, sets itself at exactly fist range from it, jabs, and steps back out of reach while the fists recharge.

name: Jack
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Dreadnought), including the champion.
idea: Lever from round 1 with the two faults its fights showed put right: axles of thick steel, since Lever lost two of three just landing on rough ground, and a fork that stays under the enemy and keeps carrying instead of letting go after four seconds. Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Sparrer
why: Knocked out by Jab in 36.8 s (ring_out).
idea: Jab on legs. Jab's wheels stalled on the hills and it drew two of its four fights standing off. This puts the same three piston fists and the same leg-picking program on the league's six-legged steel frame, to see whether the boxer works on ground that wheels cannot take.

name: Toss
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Jab, Warden), including the champion.
idea: A flipper, to end the draws. Thick-steel machines shrug off every blow in the league, so this one does not try to break them: it slides three steel pads under the enemy and fires them upward together on geared pistons, 30 kN in all, enough to throw a 700 kg machine off its feet. Then it drives the tumbling machine out before it recovers.

name: Fencer
idea: Reach. A six-legged walker with one piston point on the end of a long steel shaft, 3.5 m ahead of its core and 4.1 m at full thrust, against Jab's 2.5 m. It keeps its target at exactly that distance, thrusts when it is lined up, and gives ground when anything comes inside the point, so the enemy is always walking onto it.

name: Hornet-flank
idea: Hornet's body with a program that picks its side. It works out where the enemy's weapons are from the enemy's own moving joints, circles to the opposite side at full speed, staying out of reach, and only then runs in. The turret tracks the nearest piece it can actually hit, not the enemy's middle, and it leaves along the same weak side, re-reading the side as the enemy turns.

name: Jab-flank
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Jab), including the champion.
idea: Jab's body with a program that will not step in from the front. It reads where the enemy's weapons are from its moving joints, circles to the other side, and takes only legs on that side, so it boxes from where the enemy cannot answer.

name: Ballista
why: Ballista's control program threw an error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')
idea: A ring-out gun, aimed at Toss. Three geared pistons side by side fire as one: 30 kN for 0.6 m, enough to send an 800 kg machine back at several metres a second. The program does not waste it: it holds fire until the enemy stands between its ram and an edge within reach of the throw, then fires all three. On ten legs and nearly a tonne, so the recoil moves the enemy and not itself.

name: Whirl
why: Knocked out by Toss in 35.2 s (ring_out).
idea: The quick two-wheeled body with a weapon that needs no recharge: a steel bar spinning flat above its wheels. Under the new damage rules only fast contacts count, and the tip of this bar is always fast. It goes round to the enemy's weak side and grazes it with the tip of the bar, keeping its own body a bar's length away.

name: Hornet-shadow
idea: Hornet-flank landed its punches but spent most of each fight running in and out, and drew with Dreadnought after taking four legs. This program does not leave: it takes station just outside the enemy's outermost piece on its weak side, holds there as the enemy turns (it is three times as fast), and punches every time the fist recharges. It gives ground only when one of the enemy's weapons swings to within reach of it.

name: Scythe
why: Knocked out by Toss in 41.2 s (ring_out).
idea: A walker whose weapon is a swept bar, placed by angle. A 2.2 m steel bar is pivoted ahead of its nose at leg height and driven by a motor that goes to the angle it is told. The program cocks the bar out to one side, steps until an enemy leg is inside the arc, and sweeps to the other side, so the bar comes through the legs sideways at over 15 m/s. Then it sweeps back. No pistons to recharge and nothing spinning to tangle.

name: Ballista-drum
idea: Ballista held its fire for a whole fight waiting for the enemy to stand within 4.5 m of an edge, and drew four times without firing once. This program fires every time the rams are charged and on target with an edge anywhere behind the enemy, so each salvo walks it a few metres further out.

name: Stoat
idea: The shadowing program on a body that can take a punch. Hornet-shadow put Dreadnought out of the ring but lost its whole axle to one of Jab's fists. This is four driven wheels on thick steel axles, three times Hornet's weight and still twice as fast as the walkers, with a steel fist on a turret set above its own wheels so it can punch in any direction while holding station behind the enemy. Toss's pads only reach forward, so it is built to live on Toss's tail.

name: Reaper
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Toss, Jab), including the champion.
idea: Scythe with the bar hung low, a third of a metre off the ground instead of two thirds. Scythe's bar passed over the top of low wheeled machines such as Toss. At this height it meets wheels, feet and the ends of spokes, and the program goes for wheels as well as legs.

name: Scythe-wheels
why: Won 3 of 4 (beat Toss, Scythe, Jab), including the champion.
idea: Scythe only looked for legs, so against a wheeled machine it swept at whatever was nearest, which against Toss was a pad lying under the bar's height. This program treats wheels as legs: it steps in on the nearest wheel or leg and sweeps through that.

name: Stoat-bold
idea: Stoat kept backing away from Toss because it counted Toss's pads as a threat from any side, even from behind, where they cannot reach. This program counts a weapon only when it is on Stoat's side of the enemy's middle. Behind Toss, nothing is, so it stays on Toss's tail and keeps punching.

idea: Toss with a steel skirt down each side. Reaper and Scythe-wheels beat Toss by sweeping a low bar through its wheels and taking the axles off with them. The skirts stand outside the wheels at bar height, so the bar meets thick steel first.

name: Reaper-press
why: Knocked out by Jack in 20.2 s (ring_out).
idea: Reaper drew with Ox standing ten metres away for the whole fight, each waiting on the other. This program notices when it has not moved for four seconds with nothing in the bar's arc, gives up on picking a leg, and walks straight at the enemy until something is in reach.

name: Swift
idea: Reaper's low swept bar on six wheels instead of six legs. Reaper wins by sweeping wheels and legs off, but walks at 2.2 m/s and cannot catch or get round anything. This carries the same bar at wheel-hub height on Toss's steel-axled chassis, so it can pick its angle and get the bar onto Jack's wheels before Jack gets its fork under.

name: Mower
idea: Swift with two bars instead of one, a low one on the left for wheels and feet and a high one on the right for bodies and forks, closing like shears. Jack wins by getting its fork under and carrying; shears that close from both sides hit Jack's front wheels and its fork arm in the same stroke, and each stroke is a hit with no wasted return swing on one side.

name: Swift-climb
idea: Swift and Jack drew on High ground parked ten metres apart: the shared route-finder refuses a steep slope, so neither went up. This program notices two seconds of standing still out of reach and drives straight at Jack for three, slope or not, braking only for the edge.

name: Toss-skirt

idea: Toss with a steel skirt down each side. Reaper, Scythe-wheels and Swift beat wheeled machines by sweeping a low bar through the wheels and taking the axles off with them. The skirts are two thick steel rails outside the wheels at bar height, so the bar meets them first.

name: Jack-arc
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Mantis), including the champion.
idea: A slow-motion look at the High ground stand-offs showed the cause: a six-wheeled machine with all its wheels on the ground cannot turn on the spot. The tyres grip too well to scrub sideways, so when the way to the enemy is round the hill it sits with its wheels fighting each other. Jack leads on draws because of this. Jack-arc keeps Jack as built and changes the steering: it never asks for a turn on the spot, and turns in a moving arc instead.

name: Pivot
why: Won 4 of 4 (beat Mantis, Jack, Dreadnought, Toss), including the champion.
idea: A slow-motion look at the High ground stand-offs showed the cause: a six-wheeled machine with all its wheels on the ground cannot turn on the spot. The tyres grip too well to scrub sideways, so when the way to the enemy is round the hill it sits with its wheels fighting each other. Pivot is Mower with the middle axle set lower, so it rocks on two wheels and turns freely. Against Mantis that should let it keep its shears pointed at Mantis instead of being walked round and shoved out.

name: Toss-rocker
idea: A slow-motion look at the High ground stand-offs showed the cause: a six-wheeled machine with all its wheels on the ground cannot turn on the spot. The tyres grip too well to scrub sideways, so when the way to the enemy is round the hill it sits with its wheels fighting each other. Toss-rocker is Toss with the middle axle set lower. Same pads, same program; the only change is that it can turn.

name: Jack-rocker
idea: Jack drew five fights because it could not turn to face what it was chasing. Jack-rocker is Jack with the middle axle set lower so it rocks on two wheels and turns on the spot. If it can face Pivot it can get the fork under the shears and carry Pivot out.

name: Lance
idea: Pivot wins with two 1.9 m bars. Lance is Swift on the same rocker axle, with one 2.2 m bar hung low: it can turn as well as Pivot and its bar lands first, on the front wheels of Pivot and the yoke its shears hang from.

name: Pivot-flank
idea: Pivot can turn now, so let it choose its side. It works out where the enemy's weapons are, and goes for the wheel or leg furthest round on the other side, instead of whatever is nearest, which is usually the weapon itself.

idea: Every six-wheeled machine loses its front axle in the first exchange, about three seconds in, and the fight is then decided on who lost less. Pivot-guard is Pivot with a steel bumper across the front of its wheels and a guard down the outside of each front wheel, so a bar or a pad meets thick steel before it meets the axle.

name: Harvester
why: Knocked out by Pivot in 23.6 s (ring_out).
idea: A walker to beat Pivot. Losing a leg costs a walker little; losing an axle costs a wheeled machine a fifth of itself. Harvester is Reaper with a second bar above the first, swinging the opposite way, and a program that goes first for what a weapon hangs from (yoke, nose, brow) before wheels and legs: Jack-rocker showed Pivot's whole yoke comes off in one piece.

name: Pivot-fence
idea: Pivot against Pivot is decided by who loses a front axle first, and they lose them when the machines run into each other. This program fences: it stops at the bars' full reach, cuts, and backs straight out while the bars open, so its wheels never come within the enemy's reach.

name: Bull
idea: Pivot's bars take legs and axles, the things that stick out. Bull has nothing sticking out: wheels inside steel side rails, a steel prow across the front and a low blade ahead of it, on the rocker axle so it can turn. It carries no weapon at all. At over a tonne against Pivot's 737 kg it means to get the blade under Pivot's bars and walk it out of the ring.

name: Dray
idea: Harvester with weight. A 355 kg walker is pushed wherever a wheeled machine wants it; Dray carries three steel blocks on its back to make it harder to shove, keeps Harvester's two counter-swinging bars, and keeps to the middle of the ring.

name: Harvester-hold
idea: Harvester broke more of Pivot than Pivot broke of it, and still lost, shoved out of the ring at 23 seconds. This program refuses to fight near the edge: within four metres of it, it walks back to the middle and lets the enemy come to its bars.

name: Bull-flank
idea: Bull drove straight into Pivot's shears and lost its front axle, its blade and a rail in the first six seconds. This program goes round first: it finds the side away from the enemy's weapons, drives to a point out on that side, and only then turns in to shove.

name: Hoop
idea: Bull's rails stopped the low bar but Pivot's high bar went over them and took the front axle. Hoop drops the rails and the blade for speed and stacks its steel where the bars land: a prow two beams high across the front, hub height to wheel-top height, and a short high guard outside each front wheel.

name: Lance-yoke
idea: Lance has the longest bar in the league, 2.2 m to Pivot's 1.9 m, and drew with Pivot going for its wheels. This program goes first for what the enemy's weapon hangs from: against Pivot that is the yoke, which Jack-rocker showed comes off in one piece with both bars.

name: Maul
idea: Every bar in the league swings flat, and Pivot's two bars guard everything at their own height. Maul comes over the top: a 2.2 m steel arm on a post, cocked straight up and brought down like a hammer on whatever the enemy's weapon hangs from. Pivot's yoke is 0.45 m off the ground with nothing above it.

name: Reaper-hold
idea: Harvester-hold drew with Pivot by refusing to fight near the edge. Reaper is the better-tested walker with one low bar; this gives it the same rule: inside four metres of the edge it walks back to the middle and lets the enemy come onto its bar there.

name: Rotor
idea: A swept bar has to stop, cock and swing again; between swings it is harmless, and Pivot gets its cut in then. Rotor's bar never stops. It is centred on a pivot at the end of a boom ahead of the nose and spins flat at hub height the whole fight, so whatever comes within 1.2 m of the boom's end is struck several times a second.

why: It lost bar_r with nothing touching it.
idea: Pivot's shears on Sting's body: the two bars, one low and one high, hang from a yoke on the end of a 2.4 m boom, and the four wheels are under the back half where no bar in the league can reach them while the shears are closing.

name: Maul-reach
idea: Maul drew with Pivot but kept its wheels in reach of Pivot's bars. This program fights at the very end of the hammer: it stops at arm's length, strikes, and backs out while the arm comes up again.

name: Sting

idea: Every fight between bar machines starts with each losing its front axle, because the front wheels sit a metre behind the weapon. Sting has no front axle to lose. Its four wheels are under the back half and the bar swings from the end of a 2.4 m boom, so its nearest wheel is nearly three metres behind its pivot, out of reach of any bar in the league while its own bar is landing.

name: Heron
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Pivot), including the champion.
idea: Sting's idea on legs. Reaper loses legs to every bar in the league because they are a metre behind its own. Heron carries the same low bar on the end of a 2.4 m boom, so its nearest leg is three metres behind the pivot and out of any bar's reach, and it sweeps first at whatever the enemy's weapon hangs from.

name: Sting-yoke
idea: Sting beat Pivot without breaking anything: it just kept its own wheels out of reach. This program gives it something to break. It sweeps first at what the enemy's weapon hangs from, Pivot's yoke and nose, which sit right at the end of Sting's reach and take both of Pivot's bars with them when they go.

name: Swift-round
idea: Sting beat Pivot by keeping its wheels behind a long boom, but lost to Swift when Swift's bar happened to reach its rear axle. This program does that on purpose: it works out where the enemy's weapon is and goes for the wheel furthest from it, which against Sting means driving round the boom. Against Pivot it means the rear wheels instead of the shears.

name: Eel
why: Part "bar": its centre is outside the build box of [8,5,9] around the core.
idea: The boom idea on the biggest body in the kit. Heron is light and gets shoved; Eel is the ten-legged steel centipede frame, about twice the weight, with a 2.4 m boom off its nose and a low swept bar on the end, over eight metres from tail to bar tip. Its nearest leg is more than two metres behind the bar's pivot, and it sweeps first at what the enemy's weapon hangs from.

name: Pivot-wait
idea: Pivot's only two losses came on High ground, to machines that let it come to them round the hill. This program does the same: for the first 25 seconds it stays where it is with the shears open and only turns to face the enemy, and attacks only once the enemy is within five metres or the time is up.

name: Snap
idea: A sprung weapon, the first in the league. Snap is Sting with a spring on its bar: the spring pulls the bar hard to one side, the motor winds it back against the spring to cock it, and the strike is the spring and the motor together, always in the same direction. A swept bar does its damage by tip speed, and this one should arrive faster than any motor alone can drive it.

name: Eel-b
idea: The boom idea on the biggest body in the kit. Heron is light and gets shoved; Eel is the ten-legged steel centipede frame, about twice the weight, with a 1.6 m boom off its nose and a low swept bar on the end, over seven metres from tail to bar tip. Its nearest leg is a metre and a half behind the bar's pivot, and it sweeps first at what the enemy's weapon hangs from.

name: Heron-hold
idea: Heron has beaten Pivot two fights in three, and lost the third and its fight with Mower by being worn down near the edge. This program keeps it in the middle of the ring: inside four and a half metres of the edge it walks back to the centre and lets the enemy come onto the end of its boom there.

name: Snap-light
idea: Snap's sprung bar drew every fight, and probably never cocked: a 1500 N·m spring may be more than its motor can wind. Snap-light is the same machine with a spring a quarter as stiff, light enough to wind and still adding to every strike.

name: Jack-lift
idea: Jack-arc put Mantis out of the ring in 12.6 seconds, the fastest finish of the night, by steering in arcs. Jack-lift puts that steering on the rocker body, which can also turn on the spot, so the fork can be brought round onto Pivot's yoke from wherever Pivot turns. Fork under, lift, carry it out.

name: Pivot-finish
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Pivot, Pivot-flank), including the champion.
idea: Pivot wins on damage at the bell and has never put a machine out of the ring or destroyed one. This program finishes: once the enemy has lost two wheels or legs, it stops cutting, holds the shears open as a catcher, gets on the enemy's inboard side and drives it out.

name: Ram
idea: Four fights in ten end in a draw and fewer than one in five ends with a machine out of the ring. Ram is built only for that. It is Bull stripped of its rails and blade to get its speed back: six wheels on the rocker and a steel prow, nothing to swing and nothing to wind. It gets on the side of the enemy away from the nearest edge and drives it out.
